data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek word 'hyacinthos', which refers to the hyacinth flower. In Greek mythology, the name is associated with Hyacinthus, a handsome youth loved by Apollo and Zephyrus. When Hyacinthus died, Apollo caused a hyacinth flower to bloom from his blood. The name Hyacinthe carries the meaning “Hyacinth flower” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Hyacinthe usually hope their child will grow to embody hyacinth flower and live with faith, good character and purpose.
